extracted.intended_audience: researchers (all career levels) and facilitators interested in writing, teaching, or organising ethical and constructive peer review (manuscripts and grants)
extracted.subtask_description: Resources and templates to guide reviewers and trainers in composing ethical, constructive, and bias-aware peer reviews of research manuscripts and grant proposals, and in running collaborative 'Live Review' sessions. Includes assessment rubrics, step-by-step reviewer guides, facilitator materials, and operational templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socially-conscious and constructive composition and assessment of research manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Open Reviewers Toolkit is designed 'to help guide the socially-conscious and constructive composition and assessment of research manuscripts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing: reviews should be socially conscious and constructive. The Toolkit comprises multiple guides to assist reviewers in composing and assessing manuscripts with these values in mind (see Bias Reflection Guide, Reviewer Guide, Review Assessment Rubric). All resources are openly licensed (CC BY 4.0) and available for download on Zenodo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Reflection Guide (self-assessment of reviewer bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: A tool 'to help a reviewer assess their own biases, guiding them through a non-judgmental, self-reflective process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: prompt reviewers to identify and reflect on their biases before/while reviewing. Availability: English (original), español, português brasileiro. Use as part of reviewer training or individual review preparation to reduce biased judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Reviewer Guide (comprehensive step-by-step reviewer framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reviewer Guide 'is for anyone reviewing a research manuscript. It provides a comprehensive, step-by-step framework for the reviewer to use while they are composing a review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: follow the guide while composing reviews to ensure completeness, constructive tone, and ethical practice. Availability: English (original), español, português brasileiro. Suitable for reviewers at all career stages and for inclusion in reviewer training.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Review Assessment Rubric (evaluate quality of a review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review Assessment Rubric 'is for anyone evaluating a research manuscript’s review. The rubric comprises 10 statements for which the evaluator is asked to provide a score and a written comment to help improve the review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function: assess reviews themselves (meta-review), using 10 scored statements plus free-text feedback to guide review improvement. Availability: English (original), español, português brasileiro. Intended for editors, trainers, or peers who evaluate review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Reviewers Workshop (training objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Open Reviewers Workshop is 'a training designed for researchers at all career levels who are interested in engaging in ethical and constructive manuscript peer review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format: workshop uses the Open Reviewers Toolkit resources to train participants. Objective: enable participants to conduct ethical, constructive, and bias-aware peer review. Materials and templates used in the workshop are publicly shared (Zenodo, CC BY 4.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-specific training and templates (Open Reviewers in Africa)
rubrics_metrics.description: A peer-review training workshop ('Open Peer Reviewers in Africa') tailored to the region-specific context of African researchers; includes a pilot program recap and publicly shared templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials: trainer guide, Module I/II/III template slide decks, Module III facilitation document, Module III assignment document. Availability: English (original), français, العربية for most templates; some items noted to be translated. Purpose: adapt reviewer training to regional contexts and languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Grant Reviewers — bias-aware grant review training
rubrics_metrics.description: Training materials co-developed with funder groups 'with a focus on identifying and mitigating bias within the grant review process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience: grant reviewers (internal or external). Purpose: embed transparent, equitable, and inclusive practices into research funding review. Materials intended to support fair assessment of proposal quality and fit while mitigating bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Reflection Guide for grant reviewers (assess bias in grant review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bias Reflection Guide is also presented as 'a tool for anyone tasked with evaluating the quality and fit of a grant proposal, either as an internal or external reviewer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: prompt grant reviewers to reflect on personal or systemic biases affecting assessment of proposal quality and fit. Intended as part of grant reviewer training or as a pre-review checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Grant Reviewer Guide (step-by-step grant review framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Grant Reviewer Guide 'is a comprehensive, step-by-step framework designed to help anyone who is going through the process of reviewing a grant application proposal, whether directly invited to participate as an external reviewer, or selected through a call for reviewers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: follow the guide to structure grant proposal evaluations, ensure consistency, and apply bias-mitigation practices. Developed for funders and reviewers collaborating under Open & Equitable Model Funding Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Reviews (interactive preprint review calls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Live Reviews are 'topic-centered, interactive preprint review calls via a video conference tool such as Zoom. Outputs from Live Reviews can be used to improve a manuscript or be integrated into journal review workflows.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design criteria: topic-centered, interactive, use video-conference tools. Outputs should be actionable for manuscript improvement or usable by journals. Organisers should follow provided timeline, checklist, and templates to run Live Reviews effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Review Timeline & Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeline and checklist for planning and running Live Reviews (available in English and español).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function: procedural checklist to plan sessions, assign roles, and ensure sessions produce useful review outputs. Use alongside Live Reviews Information Document and other operational templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live review operational templates (registration, communication, collaborative writing, review composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational templates to support Live Reviews: Live Reviews Information Document; Registration Form Text Template (English and español); Email Templates for Live Review Authors (English); Communication Plan Template (English and español); Collaborative Writing Guide Template (English and español); Full Review Composition Template (English and español).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: standardise communication, participant onboarding, facilitation, collaborative writing, and final review composition for Live Reviews. Use these templates to ensure consistency and clarity across sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slide decks & materials for outreach and platform use
rubrics_metrics.description: Slide decks and materials include: 'About PREreview' presentation template, 'How to use PREreview' how-to guide (including Arabic translation), 'PREreview: Revisão aberta de Preprints para os pesquisadores' (Brazilian Portuguese), video demos, and 'Full PREreview publication workflow.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: provide materials for presenting PREreview's mission, training new users on the platform, and demonstrating the PREreview publication workflow. Useful for outreach, onboarding, and training sessions.
